title: Concurrent prefetch reentrancy + eviction hysteresis — postmortem & action items
creator: Asha Banerjee
description: Summary: During a traffic surge on 2026-03-09 we experienced elevated tail latency and recurring tenant memory amplification that led to degraded request throughput for a subset of dedicated hosts. Surface symptoms included long-running inference requests, increased GC and out-of-memory traces in runtime logs, and cascading evictions that failed to reclaim expected memory. This ticket captures the incident timeline, root cause analysis, short-term mitigations we applied, and proposed long-term action items to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: At 2026-03-09T11:35 UTC a sudden shift in request distribution caused many near-simultaneous prefetches for long prefixes. Prefetch routines re-entered the write path concurrently with the eviction controller, producing pointer churn and an eviction hysteresis loop: entries marked for eviction were repeatedly re-inserted or re-scored before compaction completed. The compactor and allocator were contending on slab metadata leading to stalls and memory amplification. Impacted tenants saw 5–20% request error rates and ~3x increase in p99 latency over 45 minutes.
timeline: 2026-03-09T11:35 UTC — Traffic spike originates from increased batch jobs in tenant T-482; prefetch fanout increases by ~8x
2026-03-09T11:36 UTC — Alert: host group hg-dedicated-6 reports growing mem_used and GC cycles; SRE paged
2026-03-09T11:38 UTC — Observed elevated eviction churn in kvcache telemetry; eviction throughput drops while in-place writes increase
2026-03-09T11:44 UTC — Multiple hosts enter degraded state; automated scaling attempted but hit reserved capacity limits
2026-03-09T11:50 UTC — Emergency mitigations applied: prefetch concurrency limited at the routing layer and aggressive eviction bias toggled off
2026-03-09T12:05 UTC — Memory stabilization begins on most hosts; errors drop to baseline by 12:30 UTC
2026-03-09T12:45 UTC — Incident declared mitigated; post-incident monitoring continued for 24h
root_cause: The root cause is a reentrancy window in the prefetch path where asynchronous prefetch completion callbacks could re-insert or update cache entries while the eviction/compaction subsystem was concurrently scanning the same slab metadata. This exposed a race between refcount updates and eviction scoring that allowed entries to resurface repeatedly, preventing compaction from reclaiming memory and driving allocator fragmentation.
contributing_factors: Prefetch fanout lacks adaptive throttling based on current eviction pressure
Eviction scorer updates are not atomic with respect to compaction markers
Slab metadata locks are coarse-grained and cause head-of-line blocking under contention
Telemetry lacked a direct signal for 'evicted-but-resurrected' rate — made detection slower
Autoscaling was constrained by reserved capacity policies, delaying additional capacity during surge
mitigations: Short-term: Disabled aggressive prefetch for tenants over a memory-signal threshold (applied 2026-03-09 11:50 UTC)
Short-term: Tuned eviction bias to favor stable low-risk candidates for 30m post-incident
Short-term: SRE removed two large batch-job sources and asked customer to temporarily lower prefetch window
Long-term: Design and implement atomic eviction-mark + compaction handshake to prevent re-insert races
Long-term: Add adaptive prefetch controller that backs off on rising eviction churn and mem_pressure
Long-term: Introduce fine-grained slab metadata locks or lock-free metadata updates to reduce head-of-line contention
Long-term: Add telemetry metric 'resurrected_evictions' and an alert when rate exceeds baseline
action_items: AI-1: Implement a prefetch concurrency governor (service-level) that observes eviction_churn and mem_pressure and throttles prefetch — owner: Liam O'Connor — estimate 5 — due 2026-03-28
AI-2: Proto design for eviction-mark/compaction handshake and API sketch for atomic scorer transitions — owner: Priya Nadarajan — estimate 3 — due 2026-03-20

AI-3: Add 'evicted_but_reinserted' counter to kvcache telemetry and dashboard panel; create alert with 15-min burn rate threshold — owner: Observability team (Carlos Mendez) — estimate 2 — due 2026-03-21

AI-4: Replace coarse slab lock with per-slab lock striping and measure contention; fallback plan to incremental compaction to bound stall times — owner: Runtime team (Jin Park) — estimate 8 — due 2026-04-08
AI-5: Emergency runbook update: include prefetch throttle knob and customer communication template — owner: SRE (Maya Thompson) — estimate 1 — due 2026-03-18
AI-6: Review reserved-capacity autoscaling policy to allow temporary emergency burst for critical tenants; propose safe guardrails — owner: Capacity team (Owen Reed) — estimate 3 — due 2026-03-25
followups: Convene design review with Runtime, Observability, and SRE to agree on handshake contract (target 2026-03-22)
Run chaos testing scenario that simulates simultaneous prefetch completions and compaction to validate fixes
Coordinate with Sales/Customer Success to notify any affected customers of remediation plan and timelines
Schedule a post-implementation retrospective 4 weeks after root fix deployment to verify regression prevention
notes: This incident highlighted a new class of race where optimistic prefetch semantics interact poorly with eviction policies under heavy fanout. Prioritizing an atomic contract between eviction and insertion paths will give predictable memory reclamation. Coordinate with Solutions Engineers to identify high-fanout tenants for additional load tests.
